prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the sloped planar geometry of the plastered masonry wall and interior corner, showing the upper wall surface at roughly 0.2 to 0.5 metres from the camera wearer (bright white) sloping away toward the floor and lower recesses at 1.0 to 2.5 metres (dark grey to black). In frames 2 and 3, the camera wearer's right hand and the wooden straightedge ruler are visible at the bottom centre within arm's reach (about 0.4 to 0.6 metres away) against the receding wall edge, while frame 4 shows a bucket and trowel on the right at 0.6 to 0.8 metres in front of the darker corner junction (about 1.2 metres deep). Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns and tilts their head downward from a close wall view (frame 1), tracks along the lower wall edge (frames 2 and 3) into an inside corner (frame 4), and turns left toward an exterior opening in frame 5 where a distant person stands on the lower left roughly 3 to 5 metres away. The depth map clarifies the continuous 3D surface gradient of the motion-blurred wall in frame 1 and the concave corner recession in frame 4 that are ambiguous in RGB alone. However, it is unreliable where the thinstraightedge blends into the wall plane in frames 2 and 3, and in frame 5 where overexposed outdoor light causes the distant background and person to collapse into uniform black with poor boundary definition.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only a single 'person' mask at the bottom centre of frame 2 and frame 3 corresponding to the camera wearer's own right hand and wrist. These detected hand regions lie roughly 0.4 to 0.6 metres directly in front of and below the camera wearer, within immediate arm's reach, as the hand holds a plastering straightedge against the lower wall edge. In frames 2 and 3, the hand enters from the bottom edge of the frame and is partially out of view where the forearm extends below the camera's field of view, before disappearing in frame 4 as the camera turns toward the corner. While the mask in frame 3 cleanly delineates the contour of the hand and fingers from the similarly coloured grey mortar and wooden tool—which is somewhat low-contrast in the RGB image—the segmentation map fails to provide broader scene layout. It is highly unreliable across the sequence because it completely misses the wooden straightedge, the bucket and tools within arm's reach in frame 4, the wall structure, and the second person standing roughly 3 to 5 metres away on the lower left in frame 5 (who is facing away/sideways and not looking at the camera wearer).
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely empty in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, rendering only a single magenta right-hand skeleton at the bottom centre of frame 3. This skeleton shows the camera wearer's right hand within arm's reach at approximately 0.5 metres distance, positioned below and slightly right of centre as the fingers curl upward to grip the wooden straightedge against the wall. The wrist extends downward out of the bottom frame boundary, while no full-body (yellow) keypoints appear anywhere in the sequence because the camera wearer's body is behind the camera and the distant person in frame 5 (about 3 to 5 metres away on the lower left, facing away/sideways from the camera wearer) is not detected. In frame 3, the 3D-like finger joint articulations make the exact grip posture on the tool clearer than in the dark, low-contrast RGB frame. However, the pose map is largely unreliable for tracking motion across the five frames, as it misses the camera wearer's visible hand in frame 2, the gloved hand holding the trowel in frame 4, and the partially overexposed distant person in frame 5.
